article_title: RBA Just Cut Rates — What It Actually Means For You

audience_mapping.pain_point: Understanding how rate cuts affect borrowing capacity and mortgage affordability
audience_mapping.rationale: Rate cuts trigger immediate action - users want to know if they can borrow more or save on repayments. High action-oriented intent.

conversion_design.reasoning: High intent users need immediate, actionable guidance. They're asking 'what does this mean for me?' - FHC answers that question with personalized numbers.

cta_blocks.mid_article: **Want to know exactly how much this affects you?** Our Financial Health Check calculates your new borrowing capacity based on the latest rates — it takes 3 minutes and shows you the actual numbers banks will see.
cta_blocks.end_article: **See your new borrowing power.** The rate cut changes your numbers. Get your free Financial Health Check to see exactly how much you can borrow now, and whether it's enough to make your next move. Takes 3 minutes.

fhc_integration.value_proposition: FHC translates the rate cut from a headline into personal impact — exact borrowing capacity, specific repayment changes, and whether this creates a real opportunity for the user's situation.
fhc_integration.how_it_solves: Instead of generic 'rates are down' news, FHC gives personalized numbers: 'You can now borrow $X more' or 'Your repayments drop by $Y per month' — actionable intelligence.
fhc_integration.user_outcome: Clear understanding of whether this rate cut materially changes their buying power or refinance opportunity, with exact figures to base decisions on.

linkedin_version.hook: The RBA just cut rates to 3.85%. But here's what most borrowers miss:
linkedin_version.body:
Rate cuts make headlines. But the real question is: how much of that cut reaches your mortgage?

The data shows:
• Banks typically pass on 60-80% of rate cuts to new borrowers
• Existing customers often see even less
• Your borrowing capacity increases, but not proportionally to the headline rate

For first home buyers and refinancers, this isn't just news — it's a potential opportunity. But only if you understand your specific numbers.

The gap between the cash rate and what you actually pay matters more than the headline. And your updated borrowing capacity determines whether this creates a real opportunity for your situation.

Before making any move, it's worth understanding your new position. A Financial Health Check can show you exactly how this rate environment affects your borrowing power and whether it changes your options.
linkedin_version.cta: Understanding your position is the first step to making an informed decision.
